Context/Background:
Sonic hedgehog medulloblastoma (SHH-MB), characterized by hyperactivation of the namesake Sonic hedgehog (SHH) signaling pathway, accounts for ∼30% of all medulloblastoma (MB) and occurs across all age groups. Cerebellar granule neuron progenitors (GNPs) are the developmental origin of SHH-MB. Germline loss-of-function (LOF) variants in Elongator acetyltransferase complex subunit 1 (ELP1) are the most prevalent predisposing genetic events in childhood MB, accounting for ∼30% of the SHH 3 subtype. The mechanism(s) by which germline ELP1 deficiency provokes SHH-MB pathogenesis remain unknown. To resolve the mechanistic basis of ELP1-associated SHH-MB, we generated a germline Elp1+/− mouse model using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing (designated as Elp1HET mice).

We analyzed multi-omic signatures in GNPs collected from P7 Elp1HET mice compared to littermate controls. ELP1 was the only differentially expressed gene by bulk RNA-seq. Given ELP1’s crucial role in stabilizing the Elongator complex (essential for efficient translation), we performed TMT-MS and polysome profiling on isolates from P7 Elp1HET and Elp1WT GNPs.
Prompt: Based on the study context, summarize most relevant pathways and leading edge genes from the GSEA results of the differential analysis between Elp1HET and Elp1WT GNPs in both TMT-MS and polysome profiling.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
A germline Elp1+/– (Elp1HET) mouse model was used to probe how ELP1 haploinsufficiency perturbs translation in cerebellar granule neuron progenitors (GNPs) at postnatal day 7.  Two complementary assays were performed: (1) polysome profiling followed by preranked GSEA (user‐provided TableS2) to capture shifts in mRNA translation, and (2) tandem‐mass‐tag proteomics (TMT‐MS) with DE analysis and preranked GSEA to capture steady‐state protein abundance changes.  By bulk RNA-seq only ELP1 itself was differentially expressed (not shown), underscoring that ELP1’s primary impact is at the level of translation/protein stability rather than transcript levels.  

Key Findings in Polysome Profiling GSEA  
Downregulated (negative NES) pathways in Elp1HET GNPs were overwhelmingly ribosome/secretory‐targeting modules:  
• KEGG_RIBOSOME (NES –2.98, adj p ≈2.9 × 10^–19)  
  – Leading-edge Rps/Rpl proteins: Rps3a1, Rps16, Rps27a, Rpl8, Rpl9, Uba52, Rps6, Rps7, Rps18…  
• REACTOME_SRP_DEPENDENT_COTRANSLATIONAL_PROTEIN_TARGETING_TO_MEMBRANE (NES –2.95, adj p ≈4.2 × 10^–22)  
  – Leading-edge overlap with ribosomal proteins (e.g., Srp9, Spcs1) plus Sec61 subunits (Sec61g, Sec61b)  
Secondary downregulations included translation-elongation and rRNA processing.  In contrast, cell‐cycle/mitotic programs were upregulated:  
• HALLMARK_MITOTIC_SPINDLE (NES 2.22, adj p ≈5.1 × 10^–8)  
  – Leading-edge cell‐cycle effectors: Plk1, Aurora A (Aurka), Cdk5rap2, Cep192, Nusap1, Cenpe, Kif11…  

Key Findings in TMT-MS Proteomics GSEA  
Strong concordance was seen with the polysome data: translation‐related pathways were the most significantly depleted, while mitochondrial/oxidative metabolism pathways were among the top gains.  
Downregulated modules (negative NES) included:  
• KEGG_RIBOSOME (NES –4.66, FDR 0.00086)  
• GO_CYTOPLASMIC_TRANSLATION (NES –5.41, FDR 2.1 × 10^–4)  
• Reactome_SRP-dependent Cotranslational Targeting (NES –5.88, FDR 3.1 × 10^–6)  
• Reactome_rRNA Processing in Nucleus and Cytosol (NES –5.77, FDR 3.2 × 10^–6)  
  – Leading-edge RPL/RPS family members (RPL18A, RPL26, RPL7A, RPS13, RPS27A, RPLP2, RPS7, FAU) plus UBB  
Upregulated modules (positive NES) centered on mitochondrial function:  
• MSigDB_HALLMARK_OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION (NES 3.77, FDR 0.0081)  
  – Leading-edge OXPHOS components: NDUFB4, COX4I1, ATP5PB, SLC25A4, CYCS, SDHC, NDUFB6, VDAC1, AIFM1  
• KEGG_PARKINSON’S_DISEASE (NES 3.12, FDR 0.24) and GO_MITOCHONDRION_ORGANIZATION (NES 4.21, FDR 0.0208)  
  – Leading-edge overlap: NDUFA9, NDUFB11, COX7C, TIMM23, MFN1, MIGA2  

Synthesis  
Both assays converge on a pronounced defect in ribosome biogenesis, cotranslational targeting and global translation in Elp1HET GNPs, evidenced by consistent downregulation of ribosomal genes (RPL/RPS), SRP‐dependent targeting (Sec61/Srp subunits) and rRNA processing factors.  Proteomics further reveals a compensatory upregulation of mitochondrial energy-metabolism pathways (OxPhos complexes, mitochondrial‐organization factors), while polysome profiling highlights increased cell‐cycle/mitotic spindle programs.  This dual signature—translation impairment plus metabolic adaptation—suggests that ELP1 deficiency destabilizes the elongator complex, impairs ribosome function, and forces GNPs to shift toward energy‐producing pathways and cell‐cycle reprogramming.
